correctness.rationale: Exact inclusion-exclusion for events of k missed types uses q_nk=(n−k)(n−k−1)/[n(n−1)]. For bounded c_n, expanding m log q_nk yields −k(log n+c_n)−k(k+1)(log n+c_n)/(2n)+O(k³log n/n²); multiply C(n,k) expansion to get the two factorial polynomials k(k−1), k(k+1). Truncating at 6log n and bounding tails by λ^k/k! uniformly controls the O(log²n/n²) remainder. Alternating Poisson factorial moments give λ² and λ²−2λ, with unique λ=2 log-term cancellation; at m=floor(n(log n−log2)/2), λ_n=2+O(1/n) gives the stated negative n^-1 term.
residual_risks: Finite checkers independently corroborate finite cases only; the explicit proof, not the log, bears the unrestricted claim.
